name: Ploy
summary: AI marketing platform that rebuilds your website from its URL and keeps working on it: AI-built pages, SEO and AI-search fixes, visitor identification, outreach and ad agents in one workspace, with a free tier.
best_for: marketing teams and startups that want an AI-built marketing site plus SEO, visitor identification and outreach agents in one platform, and are willing to move their site onto it
skip_if: you want a predictable fixed monthly price, only need a simple brochure site, or want to keep your site on your current builder and host
honest_knock: Pricing is credit-based and Ploy does not say how many credits a page, an edit or a Ploybook run costs, so the monthly bill is hard to predict in advance. The step from Starter at $50 to Pro at $300 is steep, and the HubSpot, Attio and ad integrations sit on Pro. A custom domain is not available on Free. Salesforce, SSO and SOC 2 are Enterprise only.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · Starter billed monthly with 4,000 credits a month and 1 custom domain
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-03 on ploy.ai/pricing) Ploy charges by plan and by credits. Credits are spent while Ploy is actively building or editing your site; the pricing page says a workspace that is just live and serving traffic uses next to nothing. Image generation, code generation, planning, visitor enrichment and Ploybooks all draw from the same credit balance. The Free tier costs $0, needs no card and includes 2,000 credits (the plan card says 500 credits a day, up to 2,000). Starter costs $50 a month with 4,000 credits a month, 1 custom domain family and 50 enriched visitors a month. Pro costs $300 a month with 24,000 credits, 5 custom domain families, 1,000 enriched visitors a month and the HubSpot, Attio and ad integrations. Annual billing costs 20% less: Starter $480 a year ($40 a month) and Pro $2,880 a year ($240 a month). Enterprise is custom priced and adds Salesforce, SSO, SOC 2, enterprise terms and done-for-you setup. Monthly plans can be changed at any time. Ploy does not publish how many credits a typical page or edit uses, so the real monthly cost depends on how much you build.
